```{r shared-setup}
#| include: false
#| cache: false
source("scripts/analysis_setup.R")
configure_analysis_cache(project_path("data", "a305_content_analysis.xlsx"))

# Privacy: open-ended answers are printed verbatim on this public page, so
# email addresses are redacted once here, before any table, PDF or export
# below reads A305/A306.
redact_emails <- function(x) {
  stringr::str_replace_all(
    x, "[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\\.[A-Za-z]{2,}", "[email removed]"
  )
}
data <- data |>
  mutate(across(any_of(c("A305_01", "A306_01")), redact_emails))

# LLM-coded content analysis (see data/a305_content_analysis_prompt.md). One
# row per meaning unit and visualization: a unit that evaluates several
# visualizations is repeated once per visualization.
a305_content_analysis <- readxl::read_xlsx(
  project_path("data", "a305_content_analysis.xlsx"),
  sheet = "A305 content analysis",
  col_types = "text"
) |>
  # The workbook is keyed on SoSci Survey's CASE number, which does not change
  # between exports; the participant ID shown on the pages is looked up here.
  mutate(CASE = as.integer(CASE)) |>
  left_join(
    data |> transmute(CASE, ID = as.character(ID)),
    by = "CASE"
  ) |>
  relocate(ID) |>
  # Unique meaning unit = participant + retained wording; the same unit can
  # appear under several visualizations.
  mutate(unit_id = sprintf(
    "MU%03d",
    match(paste(ID, `Meaning unit`), unique(paste(ID, `Meaning unit`)))
  ))

stopifnot(!anyNA(a305_content_analysis$ID))

a305_n_units <- n_distinct(a305_content_analysis$unit_id)
a305_n_rows <- nrow(a305_content_analysis)
a305_shared_units <- a305_content_analysis |>
  count(unit_id) |>
  filter(n > 1)
a305_n_zero <- a305_content_analysis |>
  distinct(unit_id, `Evaluation intensity`) |>
  filter(`Evaluation intensity` == "0") |>
  nrow()

# Units coded to both bivariate variants: allowed only when the response
# names both variants explicitly (rule 4 of the coding prompt).
a305_both_variants_ids <- a305_content_analysis |>
  filter(Visualization %in% c("Bivariate corner", "Bivariate range")) |>
  group_by(unit_id) |>
  filter(n_distinct(Visualization) == 2) |>
  ungroup() |>
  distinct(ID) |>
  pull(ID)
```

**Participants included in the qualitative content analysis:** `r n_distinct(a305_content_analysis$ID)`.

**Meaning units extracted:** `r a305_n_units` unique units, coded to visualizations in `r a305_n_rows` rows. `r nrow(a305_shared_units)` units evaluate more than one visualization (for example, one statement that several named plots were easy to interpret) and therefore appear once per visualization they evaluate.

Participant comments are presented in two groups. Select an **Expand** button to read the responses.

## Qualitative content analysis

`ID` links every unit to its original A305 response; it is the participant ID used on all pages. The downloadable workbook identifies participants by the survey's record number (`CASE`), which does not change between data exports. Participant wording is retained as closely as possible; themes and intensities are interpretive codes. Use the search box or column filters to explore the table.

References to bivariate plots without an identified variant are coded as `General bivariates`; a unit is coded to both Bivariate corner and Bivariate range only when the response names both variants (IDs `r paste(a305_both_variants_ids, collapse = " and ")`). Proposed redesigns are included only when they express an evaluation of the displayed visualization; suggestions alone are not assigned an intensity.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Coding is not yet validated

The units were coded by large language models with one fixed prompt (`data/a305_content_analysis_prompt.md`): GPT-5.6 Sol (via Codex) coded the first responses and Claude coded the responses of later participants (IDs 115 and above) and checked all codes against the coding rules. No human coder has checked the codes yet, so the themes and intensities below are provisional. A random subsample is prepared for a human second coder (see [Inter-coder agreement](#inter-coder-agreement)).

The coders used the neutral code 0 for only `r a305_n_zero` of `r a305_n_units` units, so the intensity scale is in practice a four-point negative/positive scale.
:::

[Download the content analysis as an Excel workbook](../data/a305_content_analysis.xlsx)

### Theme codebook

```{r a305-theme-codebook}
#| echo: false

tribble(
  ~Theme, ~Explanation,
  "Accessibility", "Usability across color vision, devices, or other viewer needs.",
  "Aesthetics", "Visual attractiveness, cleanliness, or perceived ugliness.",
  "Information integration", "How well multiple quantities are combined without obscuring one another.",
  "Informativeness", "Amount or usefulness of information communicated.",
  "Interpretability", "Ease or difficulty of understanding what the visualization means.",
  "Learnability", "Whether interpretation becomes easier with exposure or practice.",
  "Legend/color mapping", "Clarity and intuitiveness of colors, scales, and their legends.",
  "Medium compatibility", "Suitability for print, papers, presentations, screens, or animation.",
  "Preference", "An explicit choice, ranking, liking, or dislike.",
  "Reading effort", "Time, attention, or cognitive effort required to extract information.",
  "SNR visibility", "How clearly signal-to-noise ratio or uncertainty can be identified.",
  "Space/scalability", "Figure size, visual density, or ability to accommodate multiple plots.",
  "Task suitability", "Usefulness for a particular analytical or comparison task."
) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    col.names = c("Theme", "Explanation"),
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
```

## Evaluation intensity by theme and visualization type

This descriptive analysis gives each participant at most one value within each visualization–theme combination. It therefore avoids treating multiple meaning units from the same participant as independent observations. Comments coded as `General bivariates` are retained in the original dataset but excluded here because they do not identify one of the seven visualization types.

A unit that evaluates several visualizations (`r nrow(a305_shared_units)` units) counts once in each of those visualizations, because it is an evaluation of each, but it is never counted twice within one visualization. Comparisons across visualizations are therefore not independent where a participant evaluated several visualizations in one statement.

Cells with only one or two participants are shown as faded points without a box in the figure, and without a median or mean in the table. They are too sparse to summarise.

```{r a305-participant-theme-aggregation}
#| include: false

visualization_order <- c(
  "Basic",
  "Adjacent",
  "Bivariate corner",
  "Bivariate range",
  "Confidence interval",
  "Uncertainty markers",
  "Animation"
)

visualization_order_with_general_bivariates <- append(
  visualization_order,
  "General bivariates",
  after = 4
)

summarise_a305_participant_theme <- function(visualization_levels) {
  a305_content_analysis |>
    transmute(
      participant = ID,
      visualization = factor(Visualization, levels = visualization_levels),
      theme = Theme,
      intensity = as.numeric(
        gsub("+", "", `Evaluation intensity`, fixed = TRUE)
      )
    ) |>
    filter(!is.na(visualization), !is.na(theme), !is.na(intensity)) |>
    group_by(participant, visualization, theme) |>
    summarise(
      n_units = n(),
      median_intensity = median(intensity),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

a305_participant_theme <- summarise_a305_participant_theme(
  visualization_order
)

a305_participant_theme_with_general_bivariates <-
  summarise_a305_participant_theme(
    visualization_order_with_general_bivariates
  )

# Cells with this many participants or fewer are not summarised (audit U12).
a305_sparse_max_n <- 2

a305_intensity_summary <- a305_participant_theme |>
  rename(participant_median_intensity = median_intensity) |>
  group_by(theme, visualization) |>
  summarise(
    n_participants = n_distinct(participant),
    median_intensity = median(participant_median_intensity),
    mean_intensity = mean(participant_median_intensity),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(sparse = n_participants <= a305_sparse_max_n) |>
  arrange(theme, visualization)
```

```{r a305-intensity-theme-figure}
#| cache: false
#| fig-width: 15
#| fig-height: 19
#| out-width: 100%
#| fig-alt: "Faceted boxplots of participant-level median evaluation intensity by visualization type and qualitative theme, with individual participant points."

intensity_axis_labels <- c(
  `-2` = "-2",
  `-1` = "-1",
  `0` = "0",
  `1` = "+1",
  `2` = "+2"
)

# Codebook labels of the coding workbook -> visualization keys, so the axis shows
# the same names as every other figure (audit V5). The codebook and data keep
# their own labels; "General bivariates" has no key and keeps its name.
codebook_vistype <- c(
  Basic = "basic",
  Adjacent = "adjacent",
  `Bivariate corner` = "bivariate_corner",
  `Bivariate range` = "bivariate_range",
  `Confidence interval` = "triple_CI",
  `Uncertainty markers` = "uncert_markers",
  Animation = "animation"
)
visualization_axis_labels <- c(
  setNames(
    markdown_vistype(codebook_vistype, stacked = TRUE),
    names(codebook_vistype)
  ),
  `General bivariates` = "General<br>bivariates"
)

make_a305_intensity_figure <- function(
  plot_data,
  fade_sparse = FALSE
) {
  # One fixed visualization order in every panel, with empty slots kept, so the
  # columns line up across panels (Wilke ch. 21; audit V4).
  visualization_limits <- levels(plot_data$visualization)

  theme_panel_counts <- plot_data |>
    count(theme, name = "n_entries") |>
    arrange(desc(n_entries), theme)

  theme_panel_order <- theme_panel_counts$theme
  theme_panel_labels <- setNames(
    paste0(
      theme_panel_counts$theme,
      " (N = ",
      theme_panel_counts$n_entries,
      ")"
    ),
    theme_panel_counts$theme
  )

  plot_data <- plot_data |>
    group_by(theme, visualization) |>
    mutate(
      n_group = n(),
      point_alpha = if_else(
        fade_sparse & n_group <= a305_sparse_max_n, 0.25, 0.8
      )
    ) |>
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(theme = factor(theme, levels = theme_panel_order))

  boxplot_data <- if (fade_sparse) {
    filter(plot_data, n_group > a305_sparse_max_n)
  } else {
    plot_data
  }

  # Horizontal labels; slightly smaller when there are eight columns. (21 rather
  # than 24 with seven columns, so "Confidence intervals" and "Uncertainty
  # markers" keep a gap between them.)
  x_axis_text <- ggtext::element_markdown(
    size = if (length(visualization_limits) > 7) 19 else 21,
    # showtext draws line gaps 180/96 times too wide (see the caption below), so
    # 0.5 gives normal spacing between the two lines of a label.
    lineheight = 0.5,
    margin = margin(t = 6)
  )

  ggplot(
    plot_data,
    aes(
      x = visualization,
      y = median_intensity,
      colour = visualization == "Basic",
      fill = visualization == "Basic"
    )
  ) +
    geom_boxplot(
      data = boxplot_data,
      width = 0.62,
      outlier.shape = NA,
      linewidth = 0.6
    ) +
    ggbeeswarm::geom_beeswarm(
      aes(alpha = point_alpha),
      size = 2.4,
      cex = 1.15,
      priority = "ascending",
      corral = "gutter",
      corral.width = 0.5
    ) +
    facet_wrap(
      vars(theme),
      scales = "fixed",
      axes = "all_x",
      ncol = 2,
      labeller = as_labeller(theme_panel_labels)
    ) +
    scale_x_discrete(
      limits = visualization_limits,
      labels = visualization_axis_labels,
      drop = FALSE
    ) +
    scale_colour_manual(
      values = c(`FALSE` = "#333333", `TRUE` = basic_accent),
      guide = "none"
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c(`FALSE` = "#D9D9D9", `TRUE` = basic_accent_fill),
      guide = "none"
    ) +
    scale_alpha_identity() +
    scale_y_continuous(
      limits = c(-2.15, 2.15),
      breaks = -2:2,
      labels = intensity_axis_labels,
      minor_breaks = NULL
    ) +
    labs(
      x = NULL,
      y = "Participant-level median evaluation intensity",
      # Two lines, so the caption can use a legible size (audit V2).
      caption = paste0(
        "Points represent participants, not individual meaning units. ",
        "Panel N is the number of plotted participant-visualization entries.\n",
        if (fade_sparse) {
          paste0(
            "Faded points without a box: cells with ",
            a305_sparse_max_n, " or fewer participants. "
          )
        },
        "-2 = strongly negative; +2 = strongly positive."
      )
    ) +
    # Sizes balanced at the ~1100 px display width of this 15-in figure (audit
    # V2): y tick labels and caption close to the x labels, panel and axis
    # titles one step larger rather than twice as large.
    plot_theme(base_size = 18) +
    theme(
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 28),
      axis.text.x = x_axis_text,
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 22),
      axis.title.y = element_text(size = 28),
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
      panel.spacing = grid::unit(1.2, "lines"),
      # lineheight 0.6: showtext draws line gaps 180/96 times too wide, so this
      # gives about 1.1 lines.
      plot.caption = element_text(
        hjust = 0.5, face = "italic", size = 22, lineheight = 0.6,
        margin = margin(t = 12)
      )
    )
}

a305_intensity_by_theme_figure <- make_a305_intensity_figure(
  a305_participant_theme,
  fade_sparse = TRUE
)

a305_intensity_by_theme_figure

ggsave_st(
  project_path("figures", "a305_intensity_by_theme_figure.png"),
  a305_intensity_by_theme_figure,
  width = 15,
  height = 19,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 180,
  device = ragg::agg_png,
  bg = "white"
)
```

### Participant-based summary

Sample sizes count unique participants. Medians and means are calculated from the participant-level medians shown in the figure, not directly from meaning units. `r sum(a305_intensity_summary$sparse)` of `r nrow(a305_intensity_summary)` theme × visualization cells have `r a305_sparse_max_n` or fewer participants; their median and mean are left blank (shown as "n ≤ `r a305_sparse_max_n`"). Means are rounded to one decimal, as they average a five-point code.

```{r a305-intensity-summary-table}
a305_intensity_summary |>
  mutate(
    visualization = as.character(visualization),
    median_intensity = if_else(sparse, NA_real_, median_intensity),
    mean_intensity = if_else(sparse, NA_real_, round(mean_intensity, 1))
  ) |>
  select(
    theme,
    visualization,
    n_participants,
    median_intensity,
    mean_intensity
  ) |>
  reactable::reactable(
    searchable = TRUE,
    filterable = TRUE,
    striped = TRUE,
    highlight = TRUE,
    bordered = TRUE,
    defaultPageSize = 20,
    showPageSizeOptions = TRUE,
    pageSizeOptions = c(10, 20, 50, 100),
    columns = list(
      theme = reactable::colDef(name = "Theme", minWidth = 170),
      visualization = reactable::colDef(
        name = "Visualization type",
        minWidth = 160
      ),
      n_participants = reactable::colDef(
        name = "Participants",
        align = "center"
      ),
      median_intensity = reactable::colDef(
        name = "Median intensity",
        align = "center",
        format = reactable::colFormat(digits = 1),
        na = paste0("n ≤ ", a305_sparse_max_n)
      ),
      mean_intensity = reactable::colDef(
        name = "Mean intensity",
        align = "center",
        format = reactable::colFormat(digits = 1),
        na = paste0("n ≤ ", a305_sparse_max_n)
      )
    )
  )
```

## Inter-coder agreement

```{r a305-double-coding-sample}
#| include: false
#| cache: false
# Reproducible ~25% subsample of unique meaning units for a human second coder,
# stratified by the first coder's (first listed) visualization. The file shows
# the unit and the full response for context, but NOT the first coder's codes.
# It is written only if it does not exist yet, so a filled-in file is never
# overwritten. Private (contains full responses): git-ignored.
a305_double_coding_path <- project_path("data", "a305_double_coding_sample.csv")
a305_double_coding_share <- 0.25

a305_units <- a305_content_analysis |>
  group_by(unit_id, ID, `Meaning unit`) |>
  summarise(
    first_visualizations = paste(Visualization, collapse = "; "),
    stratum = first(Visualization),
    first_theme = first(Theme),
    first_intensity = first(`Evaluation intensity`),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

if (!file.exists(a305_double_coding_path)) {
  a305_responses <- data |>
    transmute(
      ID = as.character(ID),
      `Full response` = stringr::str_squish(as.character(A305_01))
    )

  set.seed(305)
  a305_units |>
    group_by(stratum) |>
    slice_sample(prop = a305_double_coding_share) |>
    ungroup() |>
    slice_sample(prop = 1) |>
    left_join(a305_responses, by = "ID") |>
    transmute(
      unit_id, ID, `Meaning unit`, `Full response`,
      # To be filled in by the second coder (same labels as the codebook;
      # several visualizations separated by "; ").
      Visualization = "", Theme = "", `Evaluation intensity` = ""
    ) |>
    readr::write_excel_csv(a305_double_coding_path, na = "")
}

a305_double_coding <- readr::read_csv(
  a305_double_coding_path,
  col_types = readr::cols(.default = "c"),
  na = c("", "NA")
)
a305_second_coded <- a305_double_coding |>
  filter(!is.na(Theme), !is.na(`Evaluation intensity`), !is.na(Visualization))
```

```{r a305-agreement}
#| echo: false
#| cache: false
cohen_kappa <- function(a, b, weights = NULL) {
  levels <- sort(union(a, b))
  if (!is.null(weights)) levels <- weights
  observed <- table(factor(a, levels), factor(b, levels)) / length(a)
  expected <- outer(rowSums(observed), colSums(observed))
  k <- length(levels)
  w <- if (is.null(weights)) {
    1 - diag(k)
  } else {
    outer(seq_len(k), seq_len(k), \(i, j) (i - j)^2) / (k - 1)^2
  }
  1 - sum(w * observed) / sum(w * expected)
}

normalise_visualizations <- function(x) {
  vapply(
    strsplit(x, ";"),
    \(v) paste(sort(trimws(v)), collapse = "; "),
    character(1)
  )
}

a305_agreement <- if (nrow(a305_second_coded) > 0) {
  compared <- a305_second_coded |>
    inner_join(a305_units, by = c("unit_id", "ID", "Meaning unit")) |>
    mutate(
      first_visualizations = normalise_visualizations(first_visualizations),
      Visualization = normalise_visualizations(Visualization)
    )
  intensity_levels <- c("-2", "-1", "0", "+1", "+2")
  tibble(
    Code = c("Visualization(s)", "Theme", "Evaluation intensity"),
    `Units compared` = nrow(compared),
    `Percent agreement` = 100 * c(
      mean(compared$first_visualizations == compared$Visualization),
      mean(compared$first_theme == compared$Theme),
      mean(compared$first_intensity == compared$`Evaluation intensity`)
    ),
    `Cohen's kappa` = c(
      cohen_kappa(compared$first_visualizations, compared$Visualization),
      cohen_kappa(compared$first_theme, compared$Theme),
      cohen_kappa(
        compared$first_intensity, compared$`Evaluation intensity`,
        weights = intensity_levels
      )
    )
  )
}
```

A reproducible random sample of `r nrow(a305_double_coding)` of `r a305_n_units` unique meaning units (`r round(100 * nrow(a305_double_coding) / a305_n_units)`%, stratified by visualization) is prepared for a human second coder in `data/a305_double_coding_sample.csv` (not published: it contains the full responses). The file shows each unit and its full response, but not the first coder's codes. The second coder codes the first coder's segmentation, so agreement on unit boundaries is not assessed.

**Status:** `r if (is.null(a305_agreement)) "not yet coded. Once the file is filled in, the table below reports percent agreement and Cohen's kappa for the visualization, theme (unweighted) and intensity (quadratic-weighted) codes." else paste(nrow(a305_second_coded), "of", nrow(a305_double_coding), "sampled units coded by the human second coder. Kappa for intensity is quadratic-weighted.")`

```{r a305-agreement-table}

#| cache: false
if (!is.null(a305_agreement)) {
  a305_agreement |>
    knitr::kable(
      format = "html",
      digits = c(0, 0, 0, 2),
      table.attr = kable_table_attributes
    )
}
```

## Summary of the open-ended feedback

```{r a305-summary-text}
#| include: false
#| cache: false
# Every number below comes from objects computed above (participant-level
# entries: one median intensity per participant, visualization and theme;
# General bivariates excluded). Descriptive only: no test is run on these codes.
a305_summary_label <- function(x) {
  unname(table_vistype(codebook_vistype[as.character(x)]))
}

a305_summary_themes <- a305_participant_theme |>
  count(theme, name = "entries") |>
  arrange(desc(entries), theme)
a305_summary_top_themes <- head(a305_summary_themes, 3)

# Direction per visualization: positive versus negative participant entries.
# "Mostly positive" or "mostly negative" when at least two thirds of the
# non-neutral entries point one way; otherwise "mixed".
a305_summary_direction <- a305_participant_theme |>
  group_by(visualization) |>
  summarise(
    positive = sum(median_intensity > 0),
    negative = sum(median_intensity < 0),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    share_positive = positive / (positive + negative),
    direction = case_when(
      share_positive >= 2 / 3 ~ "mostly positive",
      share_positive <= 1 / 3 ~ "mostly negative",
      TRUE ~ "mixed"
    ),
    text = sprintf(
      "%s (%d positive, %d negative)",
      a305_summary_label(visualization), positive, negative
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(share_positive))
a305_summary_direction_text <- function(which_direction) {
  rows <- filter(a305_summary_direction, direction == which_direction)
  if (nrow(rows) == 0) "none" else knitr::combine_words(rows$text)
}

# The most frequent theme x visualization cells in each direction, among cells
# with at least five participants.
a305_summary_cells <- function(sign) {
  a305_intensity_summary |>
    filter(n_participants >= 5, sign * median_intensity > 0) |>
    arrange(desc(n_participants), desc(abs(median_intensity))) |>
    head(4) |>
    mutate(text = sprintf(
      "%s of %s (%d participants, median %s)",
      tolower(theme), a305_summary_label(visualization), n_participants,
      sprintf("%+g", median_intensity)
    )) |>
    pull(text) |>
    knitr::combine_words()
}
```

- **Data.** Visualization comments from `r n_distinct(a305_content_analysis$ID)` of
  `r nrow(data)` participants were coded. They gave `r a305_n_units` meaning units;
  `r nrow(a305_shared_units)` units evaluate more than one visualization.
- **Main themes.** The most common themes were
  `r knitr::combine_words(sprintf("%s (%d participant entries)", a305_summary_top_themes$theme, a305_summary_top_themes$entries))`,
  out of `r nrow(a305_summary_themes)` themes.
- **Mostly positive** (at least two thirds of the non-neutral participant entries
  positive): `r a305_summary_direction_text("mostly positive")`.
- **Mixed:** `r a305_summary_direction_text("mixed")`.
- **Mostly negative:** `r a305_summary_direction_text("mostly negative")`.
- **Most frequent negative cells** (at least five participants):
  `r a305_summary_cells(-1)`.
- **Most frequent positive cells** (at least five participants):
  `r a305_summary_cells(1)`.
- **Caveat: coding not yet validated.** The codes come from language models and no
  human coder has checked them; the human second coding is
  `r if (is.null(a305_agreement)) "not done yet" else paste(nrow(a305_second_coded), "of", nrow(a305_double_coding), "units complete")`.
  The neutral code was used for only `r a305_n_zero` of `r a305_n_units` units.
- **Interpretation.** These are descriptive counts from the participants who chose to
  comment, and one participant can contribute to several visualizations. They show
  which aspects participants mentioned and in which direction, not which visualization
  works better, and they stay provisional until the coding is checked.

## Feedback export to PDF

```{r feedback-pdf-function}
feedback_to_pdf <- function(df, title, filename) {

  df <- df %>%
    filter(!is.na(feedback), feedback != "") %>%
    arrange(ID)

  comments <- paste0(
    "<section class='comment'>",
    "<div class='id'>ID: ",
    htmltools::htmlEscape(as.character(df$ID)),
    "</div>",
    "<div class='text'>",
    htmltools::htmlEscape(df$feedback),
    "</div>",
    "</section>"
  )

  html <- paste0(
    "<!DOCTYPE html>
    <html>
    <head>
    <meta charset='UTF-8'>
    <style>
      @page {
        size: A4;
        margin: 18mm;
      }

      body {
        font-family: Arial, sans-serif;
        font-size: 11pt;
        line-height: 1.45;
        color: #222;
      }

      h1 {
        font-size: 18pt;
        margin-bottom: 20px;
      }

      .comment {
        padding: 10px 0 14px 0;
        border-bottom: 1px solid #cccccc;
        page-break-inside: avoid;
      }

      .id {
        font-weight: bold;
        margin-bottom: 5px;
      }

      .text {
        white-space: pre-wrap;
        overflow-wrap: anywhere;
      }
    </style>
    </head>

    <body>
      <h1>", htmltools::htmlEscape(title), "</h1>",
      paste(comments, collapse = "\n"),
    "</body>
    </html>"
  )

  html_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".html")
  writeLines(html, html_file, useBytes = TRUE)

  output_file <- normalizePath(filename, mustWork = FALSE)

  pagedown::chrome_print(
    input = html_file,
    output = output_file
  )

  message("Saved to: ", output_file)
}
```

```{r feedback-pdf-export}
#| dependson: [feedback-a305-data, feedback-a306-data, feedback-pdf-function]
#| cache.rebuild: !expr isTRUE(params$export_artifacts) || !all(file.exists(c("data/feedback_A305.pdf", "data/feedback_A306.pdf")))
feedback_to_pdf(
  feedback_A305,
  title = "Feedback - A305",
  filename = project_path("data", "feedback_A305.pdf")
)

feedback_to_pdf(
  feedback_A306,
  title = "Feedback - A306",
  filename = project_path("data", "feedback_A306.pdf")
)
```
